analytics.ranked.method: Each type’s mean position becomes a relative weight: earlier averages receive more weight, and included weights sum to 1 within a score. This describes rank placement, not the share of works or a probability of preference. A type with fewer than 3 placed works and no more than a quarter of the largest type’s placed count is excluded.
analytics.ranked.coverageLegend: The percentage below each score shows how many rated works in that group have a recorded position.
analytics.ranked.gapNote: A gap marks a score group without enough placed types to compare. Types without a recorded position at a score are left unplotted.
analytics.ranked.unavailableTier: There are not enough placed types in this group to calculate a relative distribution.
analytics.ranked.unplacedNote: {count} rated works in this group are still unplaced, so they do not contribute a position.
analytics.ranked.noWorksAtTier: No rated works in this group.

analytics.observation.concentrated: Many recorded works share {score}/10, so this snapshot uses a narrow part of the scale. You may reserve other scores for unusual experiences, or the works entered so far may simply have felt similar. More varied entries could change this shape.
analytics.observation.separatedPeaks: Ratings cluster near {scoreA}/10 and {scoreB}/10, with fewer works between them. This may reflect two different kinds of recorded experience, or different expectations for different works. The gap alone does not tell us which explanation fits.
analytics.observation.nearFlat: Most of the scale is used at roughly similar frequency, without a narrow dominant range. You may be recording a broad mix of experiences or deliberately distinguishing many levels of quality. This describes the entries here, rather than how every experience is rated.
analytics.observation.broadSpread: The occupied scores stretch across much of the scale, rather than gathering in a small range. You may be keeping both disappointing and rewarding experiences, or judging different works against different expectations. A wide spread alone does not mean that the scale is more or less strict.
analytics.observation.ratingBand: Ratings peak at {peak}/10, with {percentage}% in the {band, select, strict {1–4} middle {5–6} appealing {7–8} favorites {9–10} other {rating}} range. {band, select, strict {Lower scores appear more often than middle or high ones. You may use the scale demandingly, or have recorded more disappointing experiences so far; this does not necessarily describe everything you choose.} middle {The middle of the scale is better represented than either end. You may record a broad mix, including ordinary experiences, or set a demanding bar for higher scores. Your own meaning for a middle score matters here.} appealing {Positive scores are more common than scores around the middle. You may choose selectively, leave less appealing works unfinished or unrecorded, or treat this range as an ordinary good experience. The library may therefore reflect a selected part of what you encounter.} favorites {The top of the scale is much better represented than ordinary or disappointing experiences. You may have entered favorites first, kept only the strongest experiences, or reserve your time for especially promising choices. This snapshot may say more about what you record than about everything you encounter.} other {The recorded works favor one range of the scale. Your selection, what you choose to finish or record, and your own score meanings may all contribute.}}
analytics.observation.mixed: Several score ranges are represented, without a dominant pattern that supports one useful explanation. Different choices or expectations may be mixed together here; more entries could make the shape clearer, but there is no need to force a conclusion from this snapshot.
analytics.media.similar: {left} and {right} have similar recorded distributions ({leftCount} and {rightCount} works).
analytics.media.higherAverage: {left} has a higher average in this library ({leftMean} vs {rightMean}; medians {leftMedian} and {rightMedian}).
analytics.media.modestDifference: {left} and {right} differ modestly in this library (averages {leftMean} and {rightMean}; medians {leftMedian} and {rightMedian}).
analytics.media.mixedDifference: {left} and {right} show a mixed difference here (averages {leftMean} and {rightMean}; medians {leftMedian} and {rightMedian}).
analytics.media.imbalance: The samples for {left} and {right} are very different in size ({leftCount} and {rightCount}), so this comparison stays descriptive.
analytics.media.closeAverages: The averages are close ({left}: {leftMean}/10; {right}: {rightMean}/10). The shares rated 8–10 are {leftHighShare}% and {rightHighShare}%.

analytics.media.couldReflect: This could reflect what you choose to record, different expectations, or how selectively you choose each type.
